# STL Blueprint

> STL Blueprint turns an STL mesh into a measured, dimensioned engineering
> blueprint — plan, elevation, section, and ISO views — entirely in the
> browser. It fits cylinders, spheres, cones, and flat faces from the raw
> triangle mesh (least-squares, not a bounding-box guess), so a 72-facet
> cylinder reports its true diameter rather than the flat-to-flat distance.

## What it does

- Reads an STL file client-side (no upload, nothing leaves the browser) and
  fits primitive features — cylinders, spheres, cones, flat planes, inclined
  faces, and axial step chains — to the mesh.
- Lays out a four-pane sheet: top/bottom plan, front/right elevation, a live
  section A-A, and a draggable isometric view, with automatic dimension
  lines and a feature-measurement table.
- Lets you click a table row, or click a dimension line on the sheet itself,
  to highlight/pin that measurement.
- Exports the result as PNG, SVG (vector line art with real hidden-line
  removal), DXF R12 (1:1 CAD interchange), CSV (raw measurements), JSON, or
  an OpenSCAD script.

## Notes for LLMs and agents

- This is a static, client-only single-page app (Vite + Vue 3 + TypeScript).
  There is no backend and no API — everything runs in the visitor's browser
  against the STL file they open locally.
- The **JSON export** is specifically designed to be machine-readable: it
  carries every fitted feature with its type, exact parameters, and fit
  residual, how features relate to each other (coaxial gaps as wall
  thicknesses, tangency as smooth joins), and a passage map of the part's
  internal voids sliced along its axis. If you're asked to reason about a
  specific part's geometry, that export — not the picture — is the source
  of truth.
- The **OpenSCAD export** hands back the same model as editable, positioned
  geometry (with a `shave()` helper for unbounded planes), suitable for
  parametric re-editing and re-rendering to a new STL.
- Source code: https://github.com/javisperez/stl-blueprint
- The mesh-analysis, rendering, and export logic lives in one file:
  https://github.com/javisperez/stl-blueprint/blob/main/src/engine/blueprint.ts
